concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create a polished, realistic flat screenshot of a complete, exceptionally restrained independent software-and-games studio portfolio website. This is website concept art, NOT a photograph, NOT a moodboard, NO device frame, no browser chrome, no perspective.
Identity: Lizz Studio. Domain lizz.dev. Real projects, in exactly this order: Never Sleep; Clankerfront; Chop Farms.
Reference images: image 1 is the EXISTING Lizz Studio mark, dark green pixel LZ with green gecko on a yellow square, use it faithfully as a TINY 28px header avatar, NEVER make it a large hero or rebrand it. Image 2 is the real Never Sleep moon app icon, preserve its look. Image 3 is the real Chop Farms green orc versus bearded human app icon, preserve its look. Image 4 is REAL Chop Farms gameplay, preserve its recognizable look if used. Image 5 is REAL Clankerfront gameplay, use only in completely desaturated grayscale. Do not mix the two games. Color may exist inside the real assets, the surrounding website is flat and neutral.
Tone: mature, professional, understated, useful. Supremely simple, no bloat, no visual effects. All left aligned. One neutral sans serif family similar to Inter or system sans; no terminal typography, no serifs, no all caps UI labels. Restrained size scale, generous but purposeful spacing, crisp legible realistic text. No huge slogan, no agency marketing copy, no invented team size, metrics, testimonials, clients, or claims.
Exact project text:
"Never Sleep"
"Keep your Android screen on."
"neversleep.app"
"Clankerfront"
"Classic isometric real-time strategy."
"Stalled"
"clankerfront.com"
"Chop Farms"
"Fantasy real-time strategy for PC and mobile."
"In development"
"chopfarms.com"
MANDATORY: Clankerfront is visibly greyed out including ALL artwork and title, but still readable. "Stalled" is a plain text status beside its name. Do not style it as active, do not add a playtest CTA.
Writing uses the SINGLE real existing blog post only, exact title "Hello world", date "Jul 19, 2024". No invented additional published posts. Header navigation is "Work" "Writing" "Contact". Footer email "home@lizz.dev". Short intro copy can read "Independent apps and games." and "A small studio building useful software and real-time strategy games."
Avoid: gradients anywhere outside existing raster artwork, glow outside existing app icon, glass, drop shadows, rounded UI cards, neon UI accents, gimmicks, page textures, decorative lines, thin dividers everywhere, grids of SaaS feature cards, oversized CTAs, fake dashboard charts, fake testimonials, star ratings, floating shapes, mock browser window, image-generation annotations. All content is a believable website page, never put concept numbers or art direction notes inside the website.

Composition A: the quiet compact studio index. Desktop screenshot, landscape approximately 1440 by 1100. One uninterrupted dark slate background #172128 and off-white #f2f3f2 ink. A centered reading-width column about 760px wide, with exact equal left/right generous outer margins. Header at top with tiny gecko avatar and modest "Lizz Studio" wordmark left, three quiet nav text links aligned right.
Under header put the title "Independent apps and games." at only 40px, on one or two lines, then the studio description at 17px, max 2 lines.
A section titled "Projects", below it exactly THREE simple horizontal rows on bare page ground. Absolutely no boxes around rows. Each row has a 56px app image/icon at left; project name and short description in middle; plain real domain URL at right. Never Sleep moon icon first. Clankerfront second with a small square crop of real gameplay in grayscale. Chop Farms third with its real orc/human icon. Approximately 115px row pitch with beautiful spacing and restrained alignment. "Stalled" appears in subtle plain grey text by Clankerfront. "In development" by Chop Farms.
Below projects leave 70px, a "Writing" heading and one plain article row "Hello world" left and date right. Footer at bottom has "Lizz Studio" left and "home@lizz.dev" right. Everything fits in the complete screenshot with a little breathing room below. This is the simplest option, a finished designer's personal studio site. No large project screenshots.
